proof:
The endpoint limits exist, are finite and positive, and give a continuous concave representative: along each side the profile is monotone, bounded above by $R$ and bounded below by its original endpoint value. Concavity passes to the new endpoints by taking limits. Changing the two points does not affect planar area or the through-source section integrals, since the section line meets each endpoint level in at most one point. The closed superlevel sets on the two sides are intervals from zero to their endpoints. Interpolate two endpoints with their levels to get the concavity inequality for $A_\pm$; monotonicity in $v$ is immediate. The arms are continuous, by concavity on the interior, constancy on a neighborhood of zero because the representative has a positive minimum, and compactness of the closed superlevel sets as $v$ increases to $R$. They are positive for $v<R$ by continuity at the source. Layer integration of $r(z)^m$ gives the first formula for $V$.

The coarea parameterization $(-q,sq)$ has arclength Jacobian $\sqrt{1+s^2}$, so the density in $q$ is $r(sq)^{m-1}\mathbf1_{\{|q|\le r(sq)\}}/2$ on the original axial interval and zero off it. For fixed $w=|q|>0$, the layer formula for this density uses an atom of weight $w^{m-1}/2$ at level $w$ and the density $(m-1)v^{m-2}/2$ on $w<v<R$. Each such level survives up to time $A_{\operatorname{sgn}q}(v)/w$. Equality of survival time with a fixed slope has zero joint measure: for the atom this is a solution of $A_\pm(w)=sw$, with at most one $w>0$ for $s>0$, and for the continuous part there is at most one $w$ at each level $v$; at $s=0$ the only possible terminal level is $v=R$, a null set. This proves the surviving marginal and the $C,M$ formulas. Integrating all levels at fixed $q$ gives the asserted constant marginal. The set $q=0$ is null.

On one side Tonelli gives
$$
\int t|q|\,d\rho
=\frac12\int_0^R w^{m-1}A_\pm(w)\,dw+
\frac{m-1}2\int_0^R v^{m-2} A_\pm(v)\int_0^v dw\,dv
=\frac m2\int_0^R v^{m-1}A_\pm(v)\,dv .
$$
The continuous part is omitted throughout if $m=1$. Finally the vertical cap $x\ge0$ has mass $V/2$ by reflection in $x$. At $x=-w$ the slope-$s$ cap gains the positive-side part $z\ge sw$ relative to that vertical cap; at $x=w$ it loses the negative-side part $z<-sw$. On either side use $|z|=w\sigma$ and integrate the surviving density over $\sigma>s$. This gives $\int(t-s)_+q\,d\rho$ with the two appropriate signs. The integral is absolutely convergent by the formula for $V$.

statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $a<0<b$, and let $r:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ be finite and concave with maximum $R=r(0)$. In defining the arms replace the endpoint values of $r$ by their interior one-sided limits. Put $A_\pm(v)=\max\{t\ge0:\pm t\in[a,b],\ r(\pm t)\ge v\}$ for $0\le v\le R$. The arms are nonnegative, nonincreasing and concave. Use the planar density $r(z)^{m-1}/2$ on $a\le z\le b,\ |x|\le r(z)$, with total mass $V$. For $s\ge0$ let $P(s)$ be its mass on $z+sx\ge0$, and let $C(s),M(s)$ be the mass and vertical first moment of its section on $z+sx=0$, with coarea $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$.

There is a deletion measure $\rho(dq,dt)$ on $[-R,R]\times[0,\infty)$ given for $q\ne0$, $w=|q|<R$, by pushing
$$
\frac12\left[w^{m-1}\delta_w(dv)+(m-1)v^{m-2}\mathbf1_{\{w<v<R\}}\,dv\right]
$$
under $v\mapsto A_{\operatorname{sgn}q}(v)/w$ and multiplying by $dq$. For $m=1$ omit the continuous part. The $q$ marginal is $R^{m-1}\mathbf1_{[-R,R]}dq/2$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
V&=m\int_0^R v^{m-1}(A_+(v)+A_-(v))\,dv=2\int t|q|\,d\rho,\\
C(s)&=\rho\{t>s\},& M(s)&=s\int_{t>s}q\,d\rho,&
P(s)-V/2&=\int(t-s)_+q\,d\rho .
\end{aligned}
$$
In fact the surviving $q$ marginal is the section law in the parameterization $(x,z)=(-q,sq)$. Constant arm intervals can give atoms in the conditional deletion time at a fixed $q$.
title: Inverse concave arms and exact section deletion records
